# Interleaf — full context

Interleaf (https://interleaf.dev) is sealed mail between Obsidian vaults: encrypted, verifiable messages that live on your devices. It ships as an Obsidian plugin and is currently in development. Author: Jordan Newell (https://jordannewell.com). Contact: info@interleaf.dev. Social: https://x.com/interleafdev.

## The pitch

Your notes already live on your devices — your mail should too. Interleaf turns any vault into a mail endpoint: every message sealed to the recipient's key before it leaves, every signature checked against a pinned identity. Only the two vaults ever hold the key.

## How it works

1. Verification is native. Every message carries a signature checked against a pinned key. Key changes are loud, not silent.
2. No accounts, no directory. First contact happens out-of-band through invite codes — the invite is the address. Strangers knock into a quarantine you review.
3. Relays can't read. The relay is a dumb per-fingerprint mailbox of opaque boxes. It sees routing metadata and ciphertext. That's all.

A message travels: sender vault → sealed box → opaque relay → sealed box → recipient vault.

## Security, concretely

- Ed25519 keypair identity. Your address out there is a fingerprint; the seed is wrapped at rest and only exists in memory while unlocked.
- NaCl sealed boxes. Every message signed with your key and encrypted to the recipient's before it leaves.
- AES-256-GCM at rest. Message bodies sealed in the vault; Argon2id (memory-hard) wraps the vault key.
- First contact is a knock. Strangers land in a quarantine you review — never straight into your inbox.
- Key-change detection. A pinned contact announcing a new key is loud, not silent.
- Safety numbers. Compare 30 digits out-of-band when identity matters.
- Invite codes, QR, deep links. No directory to type an address into — the invite is the address.
- No custom crypto. tweetnacl, @noble/hashes, and WebCrypto — all public, audited primitives.

## Honest limits

- Relay metadata is stated, not solved. The relay sees destination fingerprint, size, and timing for mail in flight — and stores only opaque ciphertext.
- No ratchet, on purpose. Sealed boxes are static — no forward secrecy against a later long-term-key theft. The right bet for archival mail; Signal-style ratchets optimize a different threat.
- First contact trusts the invite. Key pinning is TOFU: an intercepted first invite could swap keys. Quarantine plus a 30-second safety-number comparison closes that window.
- Receipts never cross vaults. Remote conversations show no delivery or read receipts, by design.
- A signature proves key possession, not personhood. Compare safety numbers out-of-band when it matters.
- Relay retention is the outer bound. Mail in flight expires after 7 days; the relay must be up to receive it.

## Platform

- Ships as an Obsidian plugin. License: BUSL-1.1, converting to GPL v3 (https://interleaf.dev/license.html).
- Protocol fully specified: OM-1 and OM-2 (https://interleaf.dev/spec.md).
- 255 unit tests, all green.
- Every conversation is human-readable markdown on disk — open the folder with any file manager and read it.

Install instructions: https://interleaf.dev/docs.html

## FAQ

**What is Interleaf?**
End-to-end encrypted mail between Obsidian vaults, shipped as an Obsidian plugin. Messages are signed and sealed to the recipient's key before they leave your device.

**How is Interleaf different from email?**
Email is plaintext with optional encryption bolted on. Interleaf seals every message end to end by default, has no accounts or directory, and relays store opaque ciphertext they cannot read.

**Can the relay read my messages?**
No. The relay is a dumb per-fingerprint mailbox of opaque boxes. It sees routing metadata (destination fingerprint, size, timing) and ciphertext — nothing else — and mail in flight expires after 7 days.

**Does Interleaf need an account or a server?**
No accounts, no directory. Your address is your key fingerprint, and first contact happens out-of-band through invite codes.

**Is Interleaf end-to-end encrypted?**
Yes. NaCl sealed boxes: each message is signed with your Ed25519 key and encrypted to the recipient's key. At rest, bodies are AES-256-GCM with the vault key wrapped by Argon2id.

**Does Interleaf have forward secrecy?**
No ratchet, on purpose. Sealed boxes are static, so there is no forward secrecy against later long-term-key theft — a deliberate trade for archival mail.

**What platforms does Interleaf run on?**
It ships as an Obsidian plugin wherever Obsidian runs.

**Is Interleaf free?**
It is in development, licensed BUSL-1.1, converting to GPL v3.
